introduction: The `git_runner` spec defines `internal/gitcmd`, a hardened Go library that wraps git CLI subprocess calls with safety defaults, uniform error handling, and typed convenience methods for rebase, merge-tree conflict detection, and ls-remote exit-code discrimination. Note: no external library Verified API section was provided; all standard-library references (`os/exec`, `context`, `bytes`, `strings`, `fmt`, `strconv`) are assumed correct and should be verified against the project's Go version before implementation.

glossary.CONFLICT: A line prefix emitted by `git merge-tree --write-tree` to stdout when a merge conflict is detected, used to parse conflicting file paths.
glossary.ErrRefNotFound: A sentinel error value returned by `LsRemote` when git exits with code 2, indicating the queried ref genuinely does not exist on the remote.
glossary.GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL: Environment variable that restricts which git transport protocols are permitted; set to `file:https:ssh` on every invocation.
glossary.GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: Environment variable that causes git to ignore system-level git configuration files; set to `1` on every invocation.
glossary.GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: Environment variable that prevents git from displaying interactive credential prompts; set to `0` on every invocation.
glossary.GitError: A structured error type returned by `GitRunner` on command failure, containing the full argument list, exit code, and trimmed stderr.
glossary.GitRunner: The primary struct in `internal/gitcmd` that wraps git CLI subprocess calls with safety defaults and uniform error handling.
glossary.MergeConflictError: A structured error type returned by `MergeTree` when the merge produces conflicts, containing the list of conflicting file paths.
glossary.RebaseConflictError: A structured error type returned by `Rebase` when the rebase produces conflicts, containing the list of conflicting file paths.
glossary.extraEnv: An optional slice of additional environment variable strings passed to the `GitRunner` constructor and prepended before the hardcoded safety variables.
glossary.internal/gitcmd: The Go package path where the `GitRunner` implementation resides.
glossary.ls-remote --exit-code: A git subcommand flag that causes git to exit with code 2 when the queried ref is not found, enabling three-way exit-code discrimination.
glossary.merge-tree --write-tree: A git subcommand (available since git 2.38) that performs a three-way merge in-memory and writes the result tree, used for read-only conflict detection.
glossary.rebase state: The intermediate on-disk state git maintains during an in-progress rebase operation, which must be cleaned up via `git rebase --abort` before the repository can be used normally.
glossary.workDir: The working directory path supplied to the `GitRunner` constructor, used as the working directory for all subprocess invocations.
glossary.*GitRunner: Pointer to the GitRunner struct, the main exported type of internal/gitcmd that wraps git CLI subprocess calls with safety defaults.
glossary.*GitError: Pointer to the GitError struct, a structured error type returned by GitRunner on command failure, containing Args, ExitCode, and Stderr.
glossary.*MergeConflictError: Pointer to MergeConflictError, returned by MergeTree when the dry-run merge detects conflicts. Contains ConflictingFiles.
glossary.*RebaseConflictError: Pointer to RebaseConflictError, returned by Rebase when the rebase encounters conflicts. Contains ConflictingFiles.
glossary.-race: Go test flag that enables the race detector to find data races during concurrent execution.
glossary..git: The hidden directory in a git repository that stores all version control metadata.
glossary.Args []string: Field on GitError containing the full command-line arguments (e.g. ["rebase", "main"]) of the failed git invocation.
glossary.ConflictingFiles: A []string field on MergeConflictError and RebaseConflictError listing the file paths that have merge conflicts.
glossary.Error() string: The Go error interface method. GitError implements this to produce a formatted string containing the command, exit code, and stderr.
glossary.ExitCode int: Field on GitError containing the integer exit code returned by the failed git subprocess.
glossary.GitError.Args: The Args field of a GitError value — the full command-line arguments of the failed git invocation.
glossary.GitError.ExitCode: The ExitCode field of a GitError value — the integer exit code of the failed git subprocess.
glossary.GitError.Stderr: The Stderr field of a GitError value — the trimmed standard error output of the failed git subprocess.
glossary.LsRemote: Convenience method on GitRunner that executes git ls-remote --exit-code with three-way exit code discrimination.
glossary.LsRemote(ctx, remote, ref): Full signature of the LsRemote method: accepts a context, remote URL, and ref name; returns output and error with three-way exit code handling.
glossary.MergeConflictError.ConflictingFiles: The ConflictingFiles field of a MergeConflictError value — a list of file paths that have merge conflicts.
glossary.MergeTree: Convenience method on GitRunner that executes git merge-tree --write-tree for read-only conflict detection.
glossary.MergeTree(ctx, base, head): Full signature of the MergeTree method: accepts a context, base tree SHA, and head SHA; returns tree SHA on clean merge or MergeConflictError on conflict.
glossary.New: Constructor function for GitRunner that validates the working directory, checks git version >= 2.38, and returns (*GitRunner, error).
glossary.New(workDir string, extraEnv []string): Full constructor signature: accepts a working directory path and optional extra environment variables; returns (*GitRunner, error).
glossary.Rebase: Convenience method on GitRunner that executes git rebase with automatic abort on conflict.
glossary.Rebase(ctx, onto): Full signature of the Rebase method: accepts a context and target ref; returns new HEAD SHA on success or RebaseConflictError on conflict.
glossary.RebaseAbort: Convenience method on GitRunner that executes git rebase --abort to clean up a failed rebase state.
glossary.RebaseAbort(ctx): Full signature of the RebaseAbort method: accepts a context; returns error.
glossary.RevParse(ctx, ref): Convenience method that executes git rev-parse to resolve a ref to a SHA; accepts context and ref name, returns SHA string and error.
glossary.Run: Core method on GitRunner that executes an arbitrary git subcommand with args, returning stdout and *GitError on failure.
glossary.Run(ctx, args...): Full signature of the Run method: accepts a context and variadic string args; returns stdout string and error.
glossary.Stderr string: Field on GitError containing the trimmed standard error output from the failed git subprocess.
glossary.UpdateRef(ctx, ref, sha): Convenience method that executes git update-ref to update a reference; accepts context, ref name, and SHA.
glossary.error: Go built-in interface type representing an error condition; nil indicates no error.
glossary.errors.As: Go standard library function that unwraps an error chain to extract a specific error type (e.g., *GitError).
glossary.file:https:ssh: The allowed git transport protocols in GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL: local file, HTTPS, and SSH.
glossary.git --version: Git CLI command that prints the installed git version string.
glossary.git ls-remote --exit-code <remote> <ref>: Git CLI command that queries a remote for a specific ref, using --exit-code to distinguish missing refs (exit 2) from errors (exit 1).
glossary.git merge-tree --write-tree <base> <head: Git CLI command (2.38+) that performs a read-only merge of two trees, reporting conflicts without modifying the working directory.
glossary.git rebase --abort: Git CLI command that aborts an in-progress rebase and restores the branch to its pre-rebase state.
glossary.git rebase <onto>: Git CLI command that rebases the current branch onto the specified target ref.
glossary.git rev-parse HEAD: Git CLI command that resolves HEAD to its full 40-character SHA hash.
glossary.git update-ref: Git CLI command that updates a reference (branch pointer) to a specified SHA.
glossary.git update-ref <ref> <sha>: Git CLI command that sets the named ref to point to the specified SHA.
glossary.git version 2.39.1: Example output of git --version indicating a version that satisfies the >= 2.38 requirement.
glossary.git version 2.39.1 (Apple Git-166): Example output of git --version on macOS with vendor suffix, demonstrating a format the version parser must handle.
glossary.git version X.Y[.Z]: The general format of git --version output, where X.Y is required and .Z (patch) is optional.
Go test command that runs all tests in the internal/gitcmd package with the race detector enabled.
glossary.https://localhost:1/nonexistent: A URL pointing to a non-listening port, used in integration tests to simulate a network/auth failure (exit code 1) from git ls-remote.
glossary.os: Go standard library package providing operating system functionality including file and directory operations.
glossary.os.MkdirTemp: Go standard library function that creates a temporary directory, used in tests to create isolated working directories.
glossary.rebase-apply: Git internal directory created during a rebase-apply operation; its presence indicates an in-progress rebase.
glossary.rebase-merge: Git internal directory created during a rebase-merge operation; its presence indicates an in-progress rebase.
glossary.t.Cleanup: Go testing method that registers a cleanup function to run after the test completes.
glossary.t.Skip: Go testing method that skips the current test with a message, used when preconditions (e.g., git version) are not met.
glossary.testing: Go standard library package providing support for automated testing of Go packages.
glossary.GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file:https:ssh: Safety environment variable set by GitRunner restricting allowed transport protocols to file, HTTPS, and SSH.
glossary.GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1: Safety environment variable set by GitRunner to ignore system-level git configuration files.
glossary.GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0: Safety environment variable set by GitRunner to suppress interactive credential prompts.

user_story.goal: construct a GitRunner that immediately validates the host git version
user_story.benefit: so that the hub fails fast with an actionable error rather than a cryptic failure deep in the call stack

acceptance_criteria.action: execute `git --version`, parse the version string, and return a fully initialized `*GitRunner` if the detected version is >= 2.38
return a nil runner and a descriptive error identifying the detected version and the required minimum
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns (nil, error) where error message includes the detected version and states the 2.38 minimum requirement
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: the detected git version is below 2.38

acceptance_criteria.action: return a nil runner and an error wrapping the underlying exec failure
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns (nil, error) describing the exec failure
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: git is not found on PATH or `git --version` fails

acceptance_criteria.action: accept any valid directory path as `workDir`; the directory is not required to be a git repository

edge_cases.action: return a nil runner and an error indicating the invalid working directory
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (nil, error) describing the invalid path
edge_cases.error_condition: `workDir` is an empty string or a path that does not exist on the filesystem

edge_cases.action: return a nil runner and an error indicating the version string could not be parsed
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (nil, error) with a message indicating parse failure and the raw version string
edge_cases.error_condition: `git --version` output is a malformed or unrecognizable version string

edge_cases.action: kill the subprocess and return an error; the constructor must not block indefinitely; the context deadline or a 30-second internal timeout governs subprocess lifetime
edge_cases.return_contract: returns (nil, error) indicating a timeout or context deadline exceeded
edge_cases.error_condition: `git --version` subprocess hangs and does not return within 30 seconds

user_story.goal: ensure every git subprocess invocation enforces the protocol allowlist, suppresses interactive prompts, and ignores system config
user_story.benefit: so that no invocation can hang, leak credentials, or behave differently across host environments

acceptance_criteria.action: set `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL` to `file:https:ssh`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` to `0`, and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` to `1` in the environment of every git subprocess it spawns
append the three safety variables after `extraEnv` so that they unconditionally take precedence over any conflicting values supplied by the caller
ignore the caller-supplied value and apply the hardcoded `file:https:ssh` allowlist because the safety variable is appended after `extraEnv`
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a caller passes a value for `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL` in `extraEnv` that differs from `file:https:ssh`

edge_cases.action: apply only the three safety variables to the subprocess environment without error
edge_cases.return_contract: subprocess environment contains all three safety variables without error; no additional variables are added

edge_cases.action: never allow a caller to override `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` or `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` via `extraEnv`, regardless of the number of duplicate entries supplied

user_story.goal: execute arbitrary git subcommands through the runner
user_story.benefit: so that all git CLI calls benefit from safety defaults and uniform error formatting without duplicating boilerplate

acceptance_criteria.action: return the trimmed stdout of the subprocess

acceptance_criteria.action: return a `*GitError` containing the full argument list, the exit code, and the trimmed stderr

acceptance_criteria.action: respect the supplied context.Context for cancellation and deadline; if the context is cancelled or times out, kill the subprocess and return the context error
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns ("", ctx.Err()) on context cancellation or deadline exceeded

edge_cases.return_contract: returns ("", error) wrapping context.DeadlineExceeded or context.Canceled

requirements.title: Rebase — conflict-safe rebase with automatic abort

user_story.goal: rebase the current branch onto a target and receive either the new HEAD SHA or a structured conflict error with automatic cleanup
user_story.benefit: so that callers never receive a conflict error while the repository is in an intermediate rebase state

acceptance_criteria.action: apply all safety environment variables to every git subprocess invoked during the rebase sequence

correctness_properties.title: Safety variables always take precedence over extraEnv
correctness_properties.for_any: any `*GitRunner` instance constructed with arbitrary `extraEnv` values
correctness_properties.invariant: the environment of every spawned subprocess contains `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file:https:ssh`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` as the last occurrences of those variable names, regardless of what `extraEnv` supplies

correctness_properties.title: LsRemote exit code mapping is exhaustive and non-overlapping
correctness_properties.for_any: any call to `LsRemote` that completes without context cancellation
correctness_properties.invariant: exit code 0 maps to (stdout, nil), exit code 2 maps to ("", ErrRefNotFound), and exit code 1 maps to ("", *GitError{ExitCode:1}); no exit code maps to more than one return shape

correctness_properties.title: Rebase never returns RebaseConflictError while repository is in rebase state
correctness_properties.for_any: any call to `Rebase` that returns a `*RebaseConflictError`
correctness_properties.invariant: the repository's `.git` directory contains neither a `rebase-merge` nor a `rebase-apply` subdirectory after `Rebase` returns

correctness_properties.title: GitRunner is goroutine-safe — no shared mutable state
correctness_properties.for_any: any number of concurrent goroutines calling any method on the same `*GitRunner` instance
correctness_properties.invariant: no data race is detected by the Go race detector (`-race`); each call's stdout and stderr buffers are independent

correctness_properties.title: Constructor enforces git >= 2.38 before returning a usable runner
correctness_properties.for_any: any host environment where `git --version` is executable
correctness_properties.invariant: if `New` returns a non-nil `*GitRunner`, the host git version is >= 2.38; if the version is < 2.38 or unparseable, `New` returns (nil, non-nil error)

correctness_properties.title: Every failed subprocess produces a *GitError with all three fields populated
correctness_properties.for_any: any call to `Run` or any convenience method that returns a non-nil error of type `*GitError`
correctness_properties.invariant: `GitError.Args` is non-empty, `GitError.ExitCode` is non-zero, and `GitError.Stderr` is the trimmed stderr string (may be empty if git produced no stderr)

correctness_properties.title: MergeConflictError contains at least one path when conflicts are detected
correctness_properties.for_any: any call to `MergeTree` that returns a `*MergeConflictError`
correctness_properties.invariant: `MergeConflictError.ConflictingFiles` has length >= 1 when git stdout contains at least one `CONFLICT`-prefixed line

correctness_properties.title: Context cancellation always terminates the subprocess
correctness_properties.for_any: any method call where the supplied context is cancelled or its deadline expires before the subprocess returns
correctness_properties.invariant: the git subprocess is killed and the method returns a non-nil error wrapping the context error; the method does not block indefinitely

execution_paths.title: Successful GitRunner construction and git version validation

steps.action: invokes `New(workDir, extraEnv)` to create a `*GitRunner`
validates that `workDir` exists on the filesystem
spawns `git --version` subprocess with safety environment variables applied
parses the raw output string and returns the major and minor version numbers
compares the parsed version against the 2.38 minimum; returns `(*GitRunner, nil)` to the caller

execution_paths.title: LsRemote three-way exit code discrimination — ref absent

steps.action: invokes `LsRemote(ctx, remote, ref)` on an initialized `*GitRunner`
spawns `git ls-remote --exit-code <remote> <ref>` with safety environment variables applied
exits with code 2 because the ref does not exist on the remote
detects exit code 2 and returns `ErrRefNotFound` to the caller
receives `("", ErrRefNotFound)` and handles the missing-ref case without misinterpreting it as a network failure

execution_paths.title: MergeTree conflict detection with file path extraction

steps.action: invokes `MergeTree(ctx, base, head)` on an initialized `*GitRunner`
spawns `git merge-tree --write-tree <base> <head>` with safety environment variables applied
exits non-zero and writes `CONFLICT` lines to stdout identifying conflicting file paths
scans stdout line-by-line, extracts file paths from `CONFLICT`-prefixed lines, and constructs a `*MergeConflictError`
receives `("", *MergeConflictError)` and uses `errors.As` to inspect `ConflictingFiles`

execution_paths.title: Rebase with conflict — automatic abort and structured error

steps.action: invokes `Rebase(ctx, onto)` on an initialized `*GitRunner`
spawns `git rebase <onto>` with safety environment variables applied
exits non-zero due to a merge conflict, leaving the repository in rebase state
detects the non-zero exit, immediately spawns `git rebase --abort` to clean up rebase state
parses conflicting file paths from git output and returns `*RebaseConflictError` to the caller
receives `("", *RebaseConflictError)` and uses `errors.As` to inspect `ConflictingFiles`; the repository is in a clean state

execution_paths.title: Rebase context cancellation — manual cleanup required

steps.action: invokes `Rebase(ctx, onto)` where the context has a short deadline
spawns `git rebase <onto>` subprocess
deadline expires before git returns; the subprocess is killed
returns the context error to the caller; the repository may still be in rebase state
detects the context error and invokes `RebaseAbort(ctx)` to clean up the dangling rebase state
spawns `git rebase --abort` and returns nil on success; the repository is now in a clean state

error_handling.condition: git version is below 2.38 at constructor time
error_handling.behavior: constructor returns (nil, error) with a message identifying the detected version and the 2.38 minimum requirement

error_handling.condition: git binary is not found on PATH
error_handling.behavior: constructor returns (nil, error) wrapping the exec.LookPath or exec.Command failure

error_handling.condition: any git subprocess exits with a non-zero exit code (generic case)
error_handling.behavior: Run returns ("", *GitError{Args, ExitCode, Stderr}) with trimmed stderr

error_handling.condition: context is cancelled or deadline exceeded during any subprocess call
error_handling.behavior: the subprocess is killed and the method returns ("", ctx.Err())

error_handling.condition: git ls-remote exits with code 2 (ref not found)
git ls-remote exits with code 1 (network or auth failure)
git merge-tree detects conflicts (CONFLICT lines in stdout)
git rebase exits non-zero due to conflict
error_handling.behavior: Rebase calls git rebase --abort internally, then returns ("", *RebaseConflictError{ConflictingFiles: []string})
Rebase returns the context error; repository may be in rebase state; caller must invoke RebaseAbort

error_handling.condition: git rebase --abort fails after a conflict is detected
error_handling.behavior: Rebase returns an error wrapping both the conflict information and the abort failure

error_handling.condition: workDir does not exist or is an empty string at constructor time
error_handling.behavior: constructor returns (nil, error) describing the invalid working directory path

error_handling.condition: git --version output is malformed and cannot be parsed
error_handling.behavior: constructor returns (nil, error) indicating parse failure and including the raw version string

symbols.name: Command
symbols.notes: Used to construct each git subprocess invocation. Cmd.Env is set to the assembled environment slice.

symbols.name: Cmd.Run
symbols.notes: Executes the command and waits for it to complete.

symbols.name: Cmd.Output
symbols.notes: Runs the command and returns stdout; stderr is captured separately via Cmd.Stderr.

symbols.name: ExitError
symbols.notes: Returned by Cmd.Run/Output on non-zero exit; ExitCode() extracts the integer exit code.

symbols.name: CommandContext
symbols.signature: func CommandContext(ctx context.Context, name string, arg ...string) *Cmd
symbols.notes: Used instead of Command when context cancellation and deadline support are required.
